intro: Spain has one of the largest economies in the European Union, powered by tourism, farming, car-making, fashion and fast-growing renewable energy.

chapters.title: Tourism
text: Spain is one of the most visited countries in the world, with tens of millions of tourists a year coming for beaches, cities, food and festivals. In some places, such as Barcelona and the Canary Islands, residents have protested that mass tourism pushes up rents.

chapters.title: Olive oil, cars and fashion
text: Spain produces more olive oil than any other country, and is a major grower of wine, oranges, lemons and vegetables, many grown in vast greenhouses around Almería. It is Europe's second-biggest car producer.
Inditex, the company behind Zara, is the world's largest fashion retailer, and Santander is one of Europe's largest banks. Spain's high-speed rail network is the longest in Europe.

chapters.title: Sun and wind
text: Wind and solar power now produce a large share of Spain's electricity. Unemployment, especially among young people, has long been higher than in most of Europe, though it has fallen in recent years.

keyTerms.meaning: Energy from sources that don't run out, such as sun and wind.
